logline: A woman born with hereditary superhuman strength takes a job as a bodyguard to a tech CEO and finds herself entangled in a kidnapping case her government-detective crush refuses to take seriously.

renewal.note: Single-season series; concluded April 15, 2017. Set the highest-rated JTBC drama record at the time. A spiritual sequel, Strong Girl Nam-soon, aired in 2023.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.1 and record JTBC finale ratings, but critics noted tonal whiplash between the serial-kidnapper thriller and the comedy-romance - an inconsistency the audience largely forgave due to Park Bo-young's performance.

pull_quotes.text: Park Bo-young is irresistible and the show knows it - it built an entire romantic-comedy scaffolding around her and was mostly right to do so.

seasons.review_body: Strong Girl Bong-soon succeeded as a vehicle for Park Bo-young's timing and charm, and the lead-three chemistry between her, Park Hyung-sik, and Ji Soo generated genuine audience investment. The finale became JTBC's highest-rated drama episode at the time. The tonal fault line that reviewers noted - a fluffy romantic comedy running in the same show as a serial kidnapper plot that is considerably darker - is real, and the show never fully reconciles these registers. The kidnapping arc, taken seriously, would be too heavy for the comedy; treated lightly, it becomes uncomfortable. Most viewers chose the comedy and enjoyed it. The show's legacy is largely as a Park Bo-young showcase and as the ancestor of the Strong Girl franchise, which continued with Nam-soon in 2023.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Strong Girl Bong-soon Season 1 Episode 1 aired February 24, 2017 on JTBC as the premiere of the 16-episode series. IMDb scored the season 8.1; the finale became JTBC's highest-rated drama episode at the time of broadcast. The RT consensus credited Park Bo-young as 'irresistible' and the show for building a romantic-comedy scaffolding around her. The premiere wastes no time establishing the show's premise and tonal register: Bong-soon's hereditary superhuman strength is demonstrated in the first act, the dual employment situation is established, and the three-way dynamic between Bong-soon, her childhood crush Guk-doo, and her new employer Ahn Min-hyuk is set up with enough economy that the show can move directly into its comedic rhythm. Park Bo-young's physical comedy instinct is the premiere's primary asset - the show built itself around her and the first episode proves the instinct was correct.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere wastes no time - Bong-soon's powers are demonstrated, the dual job offer materialises, and Park Bo-young establishes her physical comedy register within the first act. The show's visual grammar for depicting superhuman strength is immediately funny and affectionate.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bong-soon's first on-screen feat of strength - the moment the audience accepts the show's rules and leans in.

critic_note.text: Park Bo-young makes the implausible completely loveable.
